text:
sam-support: Customer on Dedicated (private VPC) hit us with intermittent 401s when calling the Redwood inference endpoint after SSO dance. Happens ~10-30% of requests, no obvious pattern.
ingrid-sre: Which ingress stack are they on? ALB/NLB + Istio/Envoy?
sam-support: NLB -> our envoy-based gateway (Istio control plane). OIDC via Okta. They see 200s sometimes, 401s other times for identical client requests.
maria-devops: Any chance Authorization header is being truncated or rewritten? Ask them for a raw capture + curl repro.
sam-support: Customer provided a curl that flips between 200 and 401. Pasted request headers (redacted):
```
GET /v1/models/rdw:invoke HTTP/2
Host: private.redwood.example.com
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJ...<long-token>...b3Jp
Cookie: _okta_session=ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ1234567890... (big)
User-Agent: customer-app/1.2.3
```
When it fails the Authorization header is simply missing in the upstream access log.
josh-eng: Missing upstream header... that suggests either (a) LB or L7 proxy is dropping it, or (b) our ingress is stripping/normalizing headers. Any envoy ext_authz logs?
sam-support: Attached envoy access log excerpt they sent: `- - - "GET /v1/models/rdw:invoke HTTP/2" 401 ... "Authorization: -"`
We asked for a tcpdump and they sent a PCAP that shows the client did send the header.
ingrid-sre: Interesting — client -> NLB shows Authorization present, NLB -> ingress sometimes not. Is NLB doing TLS termination?
sam-support: Yes, they terminate TLS at the NLB (TLS listener) and forward to our ingress over HTTP/2.
maria-devops: Known edge case: long combined header block + HTTP/2 HPACK fragmentation can cause some middleboxes to mishandle CONTINUATION frames (especially if the LB does partial reassembly or has an h2 implementation bug). If the Authorization header and large cookies are sent in the same HEADERS block it might be split across frames.
josh-eng: Can you ask them to repro with HTTP/1.1 (force curl --http1.1) or to remove the large cookie? If that makes the failures go away that's strong evidence of H2 header fragmentation being the trigger.
sam-support: They tried --http1.1 and failure rate dropped to near 0. Removing cookie also made it stable.
ingrid-sre: OK that's a repro. Short-term mitigations: 1) ask customer to use HTTP/1.1 to our ingress (works) or shorten cookies/token size, 2) configure NLB to do TLS passthrough so upstream sees client TLS (avoid LB h2 terminator), 3) we can change our gateway to accept larger H2 header frames / tweak HPACK settings if possible.
maria-devops: On our side, we can also add a defensive ext_authz fallback that checks x-forwarded-authorization if present from earlier hop (but that requires trusting the LB to set it). Not ideal.
sam-support: Customer asked for recommended permanent fix. They prefer not to change app.
josh-eng: Long-term: get them onto TLS passthrough or ensure the LB/h2 stack is updated. I'll open a tickets with our infra partners to evaluate increasing max header list size and H2 frame settings on the ingress. Also will add a short note in docs: "If you terminate TLS at a third-party L7 that proxies HTTP/2, large cookies + bearer tokens can be split across header frames and cause header loss. Workarounds: use HTTP/1.1 or TLS passthrough."
ingrid-sre: For immediate customer unblock I created a temporary policy that forces their route to HTTP/1.1 at the gateway (rollout id 7894). Please monitor for regressions.
sam-support: Customer validated and confirmed 0 failures after we forced http/1.1. They're happy and will coordinate with their ops to move to passthrough in the next maintenance window.
maria-devops: Filed infra follow-up: INFRA-4832 to investigate increasing h2 header buffer limits and to test common LB implementations for CONTINUATION frame handling.
token-bot: @sam-support assigned INFRA-4832 to josh-eng and set priority P2
sam-support: Thanks all — summarizing for ticket and customer: repro = h2 header fragmentation with large cookie + long bearer token when TLS terminated at NLB; workaround = use HTTP/1.1 or enable TLS passthrough; long-term = infra change to h2 header handling / customer switches to passthrough. Closing the support thread unless we need more data. :white_check_mark:
